column1: # INLINE MARKERS.
# Written in a page as   [some text]{.marker}   or bare as   {.marker}
# EVERY ROW BELONGS TO A CLASS (theme/marker-classes.tsv), and the class supplies
# the default shape and colour. Read that file first -- it is where the families
# are defined and where the reasoning lives.
# ADDING ONE IS A ROW HERE. No code change, no CSS change.
# EVERY USE IS COUNTED IN THE BUILD REPORT, GROUPED BY CLASS. That is the actual
# point -- a marker nobody can list is just a colour. It is what lets you ask
# "what is unconfirmed across this whole site" and get an answer, and grouping by
# class is what keeps that answer clean now that not every marker is a confidence
# claim. A terminology marker used three hundred times must not drown the six
# rows that mean something is unverified.
# COLUMNS
# marker   the token you type: {.tbc}
# class    which family this belongs to. REQUIRED. See marker-classes.tsv.
# label    shown when used bare, with no text of its own
# shape    OVERRIDE the class shape. Blank = inherit.
#          box · plain · strike · soft
# color    OVERRIDE the class colour. Blank = inherit -- and inheriting is the
#          better path: the class colour is a generated CSS rule, so one cell
#          repaints the whole family, where an override is inline on every span.
# tooltip  hover text. Say what the READER should DO about it.
# ⚠️ THERE IS NO PER-ROW `wash` OVERRIDE, DELIBERATELY. Wash is a CLASS property
# (marker-classes.tsv) and stops there. A row-level colour override already costs
# an inline style on every single span, which is why that file's own header tells
# you to prefer inheriting; adding a second inline property would double that cost
# to buy a distinction nobody has asked for. If two markers in one family need
# different washes, they are two families.
# ⭐ SHAPE AND COLOUR ARE SEPARATE AXES, and that split is the whole flexibility.
# Shape is structural -- does this thing have a border, is it struck out -- and
# there are only FOUR because a reader can distinguish four shapes at a glance and
# cannot distinguish nine. Colour is free. Any shape works with any colour, so a
# boxed green confirmation and a boxed amber warning are the same mechanism
# wearing different paint.
#   box     bordered chip, tinted background. Demands attention.
#   plain   coloured text, no chrome. Present but not shouting.
#   strike  struck through. Superseded, kept findable.
#   soft    italic, prefixed with ~. Approximate rather than doubtful.
# ✅ THE CLASS AXIS COST THE SHAPE AXIS NOTHING. Terminology needed colour and
# weight WITHOUT an underline, which is exactly `plain` -- it was already there.
# Four shapes still cover every family. ✅ AND SO DID THE HIGHLIGHT FAMILY, which
# is the second time this has held: it wanted a heavier tint, which is a NUMBER on
# an existing shape rather than a shape. ✅ AND THE FMP FAMILIES MADE IT THREE:
# `layout` is `box` and `schema` is `plain`, both already present, and the two
# were told apart by SHAPE rather than by a fifth hue.
# ⚠️ PREFER INHERITING, THEN A TOKEN, AND ONLY THEN A HEX. A token follows the
# theme into light mode and into every other site; a hex is frozen where you typed
# it and will be wrong on the scheme you were not looking at. Hex is supported
# because it is genuinely useful for a one-off, not because it is the good path.
# ⚠️ THE BOX SHAPE MEANS A COLOUR HAS TO SURVIVE ITS OWN BACKGROUND. `box` tints
# the chip with the class's `wash` of the marker's own colour (10% unless the
# family says otherwise), so the text is not sitting on the page ground -- it is
# sitting on a wash of itself. A value measured only against the page can still
# fail inside the chip, and three amber candidates did exactly that on 2026-08-05.
# Measure the chip, not the page -- and re-measure if the family's wash changes,
# because that number moves the ground the text stands on.
# 🔴 `conf` AND `gap` MOVED TO CANONICAL TOKEN NAMES ON 2026-08-05, and it is not
# a rename. `ok` and `danger` exist ONLY in the nine-token stand-in, so a
# confirmed value and a known gap were being painted by a table nobody maintains
# while every other colour on the page followed the design system. `good` and
# `bad` are the canonical names for the same two meanings, and they were
# unreachable until the validator learned to read both tables.
# ⚠️ THE TOKEN IS `accent`, NOT `accent-1`. There is no `-1` anywhere in the
# canonical palette -- the four are `accent`, `accent-deep`, `accent-2` and
# `accent-soft`. `accent-1` is the natural thing to type once `accent-2` exists,
# it validates as a legal token NAME, and it resolves to nothing: reported once
# per build and painted in the body colour. That is the `accent-soft` bug wearing
# a different name, so it is written here where the cell is typed.
# 🔴 TWO OF THE FMP ROWS BELOW WERE ALREADY BEING TYPED, AND HAD NEVER RENDERED
# (2026-08-09). Before this commit `uritp-docs` carried six `{.calc}` across
# `20-tables/import_EVENTS.tsv` and `20-tables/WORKDAYS.tsv`, and two `{.button}`
# in `10-user-experience/index.md`. None of them were rows here.
# ⚑ AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT BY DESIGN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. An
# unknown marker is NOT an error: `on_page_markdown` hands it back untouched on
# purpose, because `{ .md-button }` is somebody else's attr_list syntax and
# eating it would be worse. So an author who invents a marker gets valid-looking
# markdown, plain body text, and one line in a build report. ⭐ The same shape as
# the `danger` callout that lost its red on 08-05 and sat unnoticed for four
# hours: the mechanism reported itself correctly and being REPORTED is not the
# same as being SEEN.
# ⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE NEXT PERSON, STATED BECAUSE IT NOW CUTS BOTH WAYS:
# adding a row here RETROACTIVELY CLAIMS every `{.name}` already written across
# every site. `field` is the one to watch -- it is a plausible attr_list class
# name as well as a marker. Nothing in the fleet uses it as one today (checked
# before this commit), but a future `{ .field }` meant as an HTML attribute will
# now render as a chip instead.
# 🚩 THE LINK FORMS ARE NOT WIRED YET, AND THIS IS THE ONE GAP IN THIS COMMIT.
# `[fkOtherTable](@rel:table-other)` -- plus `@script:`, `@layout:` and `@vl:` --
# is the half that makes the report an EDGE LIST rather than a count, because the
# link resolver records source → target where a span records only a mention. It
# needs `docrender/markers.py`, which is **23,084 B against a ~22KB safe-edit
# ceiling**, so generalising `_resolve_term` into a prefix table is a structural
# call and not a data edit. Deliberately not smuggled into a TSV commit. The span
# forms work today; the link forms render as broken references until then.
# 🚫 `.value` WAS PROPOSED WITH `.vl` AND REFUSED (2026-08-09, Fiona). A marker
# for one entry ON a value list. Production MAWster already carries a VALUES
# table with `VALUES.tsv` as its catalog, so every value on every list is already
# a row in a file that RENDERS AS A TABLE. An inline marker would be a second
# claimant on data the first place already owns -- the defect that retired
# `roster.json`, `registry.json` and `app-index.md`. ⚑ The distinction that
# decides this one and the next one: `.vl` is a THING OTHER OBJECTS POINT AT
# (fields use it, scripts read it), so marking it records an edge. A value is a
# ROW IN A TABLE, and the answer to "show me all of them" is that table, not a
# report. Written down because an unwritten refusal gets re-proposed.
marker

column6: Not yet verified against a source. Do not rely on this without checking.

column1: verify
column6: Recorded once and never re-checked. Measure it before you build to it.

column1: gap
column6: This fact should exist and does not. The absence is known, not overlooked.

column1: conf
column6: Double-checked against the real thing. Trust it.

column1: est
column6: Approximate. Close enough to plan with, not close enough to cut to.

column1: was
column6: The old value, kept so paperwork quoting it can still be matched up.

column1: term
column6: House terminology. Where it is also a link there is a page defining it.

column1: hi
column6: Flagged as worth your attention. This says nothing about whether the value is correct -- if you want that, the confidence markers are the ones that mean it.

column1: button
column6: A button on a FileMaker layout. The marked text is what the button SAYS, so it can be found by reading the label the way a user would.

column1: field
column6: A field placed on a layout. Names the object the user types into, not the underlying schema field -- for that, look the table up.

column1: calc
column6: A calculated value. NOTHING in FileMaker lists every calc in a file, so this marker is the only register there is -- the build report is where you read them all at once.

column1: rel
column6: A relationship between tables. The Graph shows it; nothing lists it as text. Where the other table has a page, prefer the link form so the report records the edge and not just the mention.

column1: trigger
column6: A script trigger. Nothing enumerates these either, and they are the objects most likely to be forgotten -- if it fires, mark it.

column1: global
column6: A global field or a $$variable. Scattered across a solution by nature; this is the only place they can be counted.

column1: vl
column6: A value list. Manage > Value Lists does enumerate these, so this marker is not the register -- it is here to record WHO USES IT, which is the part FileMaker cannot show you.
